title: Draw a baby carrier's cloth canopy forward to its stop over the doll's face, steadying the rocking carrier by its handle
instruction: Shade the baby: with your left hand hold the carrier steady by its carry handle, and with your right hand take the canopy's front bow and draw it forward until it stops, its front edge over the doll's face, without the fabric touching the face.
context: A Graco SnugRide 35 Lite LX infant car-seat carrier stands on the bench with a baby doll lying in it, its open front facing the robot. Its cloth canopy, sewn over three hinged bows, is folded back over the doll's head. A carer shades the baby by drawing the canopy's front edge forward until the canopy stops; Graco lists the canopy as multi-position (https://www.gracobaby.com/shop/car-seats/infant-car-seats/snugride-35-lite-lx-infant-car-seat/SAP_2110187.html) and Target the carrier at 27.4 x 15.5 x 18.07 in (https://www.target.com/p/graco-snugride-35-lite-lx-infant-car-seat/-/A-79436026). The carrier's base is curved, so the pull rocks it unless the other hand holds the carry handle, which is turned back behind the head end. The hard part is the draw: the front bow is swung through its arc while the fabric unfolds and drags the other bows after it, and the carrier must not rock while it does. Graco and SnugRide are named for identification only.
setup: Station: two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of a 120 x 90 cm wood table, 75 cm high. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Carrier: a Graco SnugRide 35 Lite LX infant car-seat carrier at its listed 69.6 x 39.4 x 45.9 cm (Target's 27.4 x 15.5 x 18.07 in, read as length, width and height to the canopy's top): shell 69.6 cm long and 39.4 cm wide, its rim 28 cm high, on a curved rocker base of 42 cm radius; carrier 3.6 kg and doll 1 kg. It stands with its middle at x 16, y 0, its long axis along x, its head end away from the robot (x 51) and its open front toward it. It rocks fore and aft on its base. Carry handle: turned back behind the head end, its side arms (2 cm square) at y 24.7 and y -24.7, 20 cm high, from x 34 to x 60, joined by a grip bar at x 60. Canopy: three bows of 16 mm tube on one hinge axis across the shell at x 38, 28 cm high; each bow is an arch 39.4 cm wide and 17.9 cm high over the axis. At the start the rear, middle and front bows lean 60, 30 and 0 degrees back from upright (the front bow upright, its top at x 38, 45.9 cm high); the front bow stops at 45 degrees forward of upright, where it clicks into place; this fully drawn position, the last the canopy reaches, is what counts as its stop (assumed at 45 degrees and unsourced: Graco lists a multi-position canopy but gives no angle; a real trial uses the carrier's own fully open click). The canopy pulls its front bow back toward closed, about 1.2 N m at the stop, so the draw takes a firm, steady pull. Fabric: polyester canopy cloth, pleated between the bows and sewn to them. Doll: a soft-bodied vinyl baby doll, 45 cm long and 1 kg, lying on its back, head toward the canopy, head 14 cm across centred at x 30, 22.5 cm high; the face zone is a 12 x 14 cm patch over the face, from x 23 to x 37 and y -6 to y 6, about 27 cm high. The line for the canopy's front edge is set from the doll's face: x 26.5, 3.5 cm past the centre of the face toward the doll's feet (11.5 cm nearer the robot than the hinge). Both grippers start at the arms' ready pose. Start state, the same every trial: canopy folded back, carrier level and still.
scoring: Read from video, with a tape for the front edge's line and a phone level on the shell for the rock: a level app that logs its maximum, or the level's screen kept in the trial video. Score 0 if the canopy's fabric touches the doll's face or a hand touches the doll (in the simulation: any fabric within 1 cm of the face zone, or any fingertip within 1 cm of the doll, at any time), or if the carrier rocks more than 6 degrees. The carrier counts as unsteadied if it rocks 3 degrees or more at any time, or is 1 degree or more off level at the end: an unsteadied run gets no credit for the canopy and scores at most 0.25. Otherwise: 1.0 when the front bow is at its stop (within 2 degrees) with the front edge past the line and the carrier under 1 degree, held for 1 s; 0.5 when the bow reached its stop past the line but was not held there steady for 1 s; 0.25 when the front edge was drawn at least 5 cm forward; 0 otherwise. With no steadying hand the same draw scores 0.25 in the simulator: the carrier tilts 2.5 degrees and stays tilted, and the bow stops short of its stop.
fidelity: Carrier at Graco's listed size; doll 1 kg. The canopy is cloth: a sewn surface-FEM sheet pleated between three rigid hinged bows (0.6 mm, 160 g/m2, 2 MPa assumed). The pull back on the front bow is a hinge torque in code (1.5 N m/rad), heavier than a real canopy's fabric so the carrier needs steadying; the stop's click is a latch. Rocker: a hinge at its bench contact, m g (R - h) = 11.3 N m/rad. The right hand holds the front bow by friction alone, 25 N per finger.
scores: Scripted demo 1.0 on GPU physics: bow drawn to its 45 degree stop by friction alone, edge 12.6 cm, fabric 10.8 cm from the face, rock peak 1.7 degrees. Lazy: nothing 0; one hand 0.25; one hand then let go 0.25. Dream-1: 0 (did not draw the canopy; rock 1.9 degrees).
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Between real trials fold the canopy back with the front bow upright and level the carrier.
